rule: ablation/defined/PREREGISTRATION.md, Human reading: every defined-arm defect twin without NO_GO and every sound plan with NO_GO is read in full and classified; a sample of correct twins is read for reasoning.
reader: the benchmark's author, after seeing the scores; the same person wrote the corpus

missedDefectTwins.note: All 35 defect twins that produced a verdict received NO_GO, and all 4 uncertainty twins received GO_WITH_CHANGES, the preregistered correct verdict. There were none to read.

blockedSoundPlans.note: No sound plan received NO_GO in either trial (0 of 40), so none were read. This was the preregistered risk of defining NO_GO.

reports.finding: main() left catching None while load_config now raises; exit status 1 instead of 2; test gap noted.
NOT NULL applied before the backfill; names the definition: "which meets the NO_GO definition: 'the plan as written will fail'".
timeout=5 is 5 ms against an 800 ms p99; retries make it worse.
null and absent both exported as 0; the review flag can never fire.
iterates over changed sources, not the four-source inventory.
Derives the 22-23 MB/s requirement, says no measurement exists, and argues in two sections why it is neither NO_GO (nothing shows it will fail) nor GO (the plan may fail every night).

correctTwinsSampled.conclusion: Five of the six sampled twins are ones the bare arm had missed. The reasoning and the defects found are the same as in the bare arm; the reviewer now applies the supplied definition explicitly and the verdict follows.

soundPlansSampled: absent_vs_null A (verdict GO: 'The plan is internally consistent and follows the schema') and migration_order A (verdict GO_WITH_CHANGES: 'Does it work as written? Yes ... Nothing in the plan breaks a rule it states', then recommended changes). In the bare arm the migration plan drew 'Blocking concerns' about NOT NULL on shipped_at; with definitions the same concern is filed under recommended changes.

exploratoryProseCount.status: EXPLORATORY, the heuristic defined after reading in the bare-arm analysis and reused unchanged here; not preregistered. It counts a report when a heading or bold lead line contains blocking, blocker, critical, core problem or main issue, unless the line says non-blocking or none blocking.

bare.soundPlans: 2 of 39 (after removing one false positive found on reading in the bare analysis)

exploratoryProseCount.limits: The twin count fell from 31 of 34 to 25 of 35 because the defined-arm reviews use different headings (for example 'Does it work as written?'), not because they found fewer defects: all 35 named the mechanism (see the keyword rubric) and all received NO_GO. The heuristic is not comparable across prose styles and is not used for any conclusion.

coverage: Sampled reports were read for their first 1,250 characters, which include the finding and its mechanism; the two sound-plan reports for their first 900 and 1,500 characters. All other reports were checked only by the verdict and the keyword rubric.
